newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch government gives up hope of Fokker resurrection.
newsitem.headline: Dutch government gives up hope of Fokker resurrection.

text.p: The Dutch government said Wednesday it saw no chance of restarting bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker after industrial group Stork pulled out of a rescue plan earlier this month.

"After a thorough assessment, the state has concluded that the scenario, given recent developments, no longer has the support base for a responsible restart of Fokker," Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers wrote in a letter to parliament.
"The state has therefore decided to withdraw as of today its commitment to take a substantial direct participation in the restart," Wijers added.
The letter followed remarks by Fokker's administrators and the Malaysian government, another party concerned in the survival plan, that the final end of the Dutch aircraft maker was looming.

Fokker's administrators, the Dutch government, industrial investment firm Deleye Investment Group and Malaysian government investment arm Khazanah Nasional Berhad reached a memorandum of understanding on Fokker's relaunch in March.
But Stork, owner of Fokker's profitable maintenance and components units, withdrew from the scheme in early April, saying Khazanah had not guaranteed sufficient financial support.
Wijers said that after Stork's withdrawal, DIG Chairman Andre Deleye had tried to find another relaunch partner.
"But it has to be concluded that these efforts have not resulted in a clear signal from which concrete interest by another industry partner could appear," the minister said.
